messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P0 — hosted runtime: sudden KV-cache memory growth leading to OOMs on hosted-us-west-2 inference pool. Paging @tara (oncall). Runbook: /runbooks/kvcache-oom
tara (oncall): acked — jumping in. seeing repeated OOM kills on gpu-3/4 in the pool, cluster node memory at 98%.
mike (eng-runtime): visible in metrics: 3.2x increase in KV-cache size across sessions starting ~2312345200. 95p latency + errors spiking. likely long prompts / prefix amplification.
priya (sre): grabbing logs. oom-kill excerpts:
```
[pid 12345] Out of memory: Killed process 9876 (inference_runtime) total-vm: 3240000kB, anon-rss: 2900000kB
Stack: kvcache::reserve_at_sequence(...)
```

sam (support): incoming customer reports: elevated 502s for hosted API. small cohort of customers reporting errors since ~10:06 UTC.
mike (eng-runtime): on quick triage, root cause seems like a continuous-batching regression + long prompt sessions that cause unbounded KV growth. There's an index bug in the new prefetch controller allowing window extensions beyond configured max.
tara (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) clamp max per-session KV tokens at the API gateway for hosted pool; 2) rollback prefetch controller config update; 3) scale up eviction aggressively on affected nodes. Doing step 1 now.
dev-bot: ci deploy started: hotpatch/kvcap-clamp-2312345678 -> canary (2 nodes)
mike (eng-runtime): command used:
```bash
redwoodctl runtime patch --pool hosted-us-west-2 --env KVCACHE_MAX_SESSION_TOKENS=512 --rolling
```

(dev-bot) deploy logs: canary success on node gpu-7, healthchecks ok.
priya (sre): taking node gpu-3 offline for investigation. triggering eviction:
```bash
ssh ops@gpu-3 'systemctl stop inference-runtime && rm -f /var/lib/kvcache/*'
```

sam (support): update for affected customers: we’ve posted a status message to the dashboard. tagging top-10 customers who hit 502s for proactive outreach. current ETA for mitigation: 15 min.
mike (eng-runtime): pushing a patch to prefetch controller to enforce max_window_tokens at admission time. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/5982 — will apply to canary after quick review.
nate (product): any indication if this was triggered by a platform release or customer behavior? we need customer impact details for comms.
mike (eng-runtime): preliminary: a small number of sessions (~120 active sessions) had prompts that contained repeated long system messages + user history leading to sequence lengths > 75k tokens. combined with a new batching heuristic, it amplified prefetch windows.
priya (sre): error rate graph: 502 rate peaked at 11.2% at 2312345290, baseline ~0.1%. nodes crashed: gpu-3 & gpu-4 both OOMed and restarted — that caused rate spike.
(dev-bot) canary patch applied: prefetch admission clamp enabled on canary nodes.
mike (eng-runtime): canary looks stable. rolling to remainder of pool with the patch + env clamp.
tara (oncall): rolling now. monitoring tail latency and error rate. marking incident channel with :rotating_light: and assigning handoff if needed.
sam (support): initial customer impact tally: ~27 customers affected briefly, top 5 saw increased errors for median 12m, worst-case 22m. logging correlation keys attached to support tickets.
priya (sre): after roll, error rate dropped to 0.5% within 3m and back to baseline by 2312345900. memory usage returned to normal. no further OOMs observed.
mike (eng-runtime): root-cause summary for postmortem: regression in continuous-batching/prefetch admission allowed window extension beyond configured max when certain tokenization boundary patterns appear. combined with a surge of long prompts caused KV cache growth beyond capacity -> OOM.
tara (oncall): current status: mitigated. Canaries and full pool patched. No active OOMs. Moving to recovery. Leaving channel open for handoff to @priya for post-incident cleanup and postmortem.
priya (sre): taking over. next steps: collect heap dumps from crashed nodes, run synthetic workload to reproduce, add telemetry alert for per-session KV growth > 1M tokens, and create automatic clamp in admission path.
nate (product): recommend we prepare a short customer note summarizing impact and remediation; asking marketing/comm to review.
sam (support): will send targeted messages to affected customers this hour. submitting incident summary to ops-comm.
priya (sre): handoff: I'm primary for postmortem. @tara — thanks for rapid mitigation. marking as resolvable and scheduling deep-dive tomorrow.
tara (oncall): thanks team. tagging incident-bot: create incident ticket with severity=P0, duration=~14m, affected_customers=27, mitigation=env-clamp+prefetch-patch, followups=[postmortem, telemetry, config-hardening]. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Created incident #INC-2023-5789. Link: /incidents/INC-2023-5789
mike (eng-runtime): one more note — long-term fix: remove admission-time heuristics that can amplify windows and add unit tests for token-boundary edge cases. I'll include in the patch backlog.
priya (sre): closing notes: all services healthy, follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC for RC/POC of improvements. logs and artifacts attached to the incident ticket.
sam (support): customer outreach drafts ready; will wait for product signoff.
dev-bot: automated post-incident telemetry check queued: runbook step verified.
priya (sre): closing thread. if anything else crops up, reopen.
